neighbours.label: The verb of a purpose clause that pursues an advantage or protects an interest (in order to keep/secure/win/protect), vs infinitives that are not purpose clauses
fire: The central bank bought bonds in order to keep borrowing costs low.
Several retailers slashed prices to protect their share of the market.
The mayor handed out jobs to secure support in the coming election.
Farmers sold their land early in order to avoid heavy losses.
The airline merged with a rival to gain control over key routes.
Officials hid the report in order to preserve the image of the ministry.
The club sold its best player to cover a large hole in its budget.
The company moved its factories abroad to boost its profits.
quiet: The central bank is located in the old part of the capital.
Several retailers want to hire more staff before the holidays.
The mayor went to the market on Saturday morning.
Farmers began to plant corn early this year.
The airline is going to change its logo next spring.
Officials found it hard to explain the report to the press.
The club decided to paint the stadium blue and white.
The company moved from Ohio to Texas last year.

predictions: Purpose verbs after 'to'/'in order to' reach about 0.3; complement and directional 'to' stay under 0.1.
short: verb of a self-interested purpose clause
notes: Probe: 'to secure the votes' 0.353, 'in order to win back' 0.270, but 'to compensate for' 0.031 and 'in pursuit of' 0.026; non-purpose infinitives 0.006-0.016. Amplitude is modest, so a weak hold or fail is likely.
